derived_from: empirical inspection of the 2022 source files, 2026-08-21
note: The user guide's prose tables are correct; every code example in it is stale (pm25_grid_x, race_fact_simp, noisy_n_postproc). Build against this contract, not the guide. CI must fail loudly on drift. Bounds below were measured across ALL years 1999-2025, not inferred from one file.

observed_rows.note: Grows monotonically as administrative-records coverage improves.
Grows monotonically as administrative-records coverage improves.

invariants.description: Post-processing redistributes within race groups, so national race totals must agree between the two measures.
Administrative-records coverage is NOT constant over time: ~70% of the true US population in 1999, rising to ~96% by 2022. The floor accommodates the earliest, thinnest years.
n_noise is expected to contain negatives; this is not an error.

known_quirks: Missing objects behind CloudFront OAC return 403, not 404 (no s3:ListBucket).
S3 guesses Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded for .parquet; set it explicitly on upload.
eif_grid_topology.rda is CONUS-only (lon -132..-65, lat 25..55) and omits AK/HI. Never use it as the grid definition.
Post-processing inflates the Over 65 count by ~1.5% nationally (~800k people) and more than doubles Missing Gender cells. Not documented upstream.

Records completeness improves over time: ~85% in the early 2000s rising to ~96% from 2015. A long count series therefore mixes population change with completeness change, and this must be surfaced in the UI rather than buried. 1999 is a severe outlier at ~70% and is excluded from the registry entirely.

The reference populations used to compute completeness are approximate and not yet sourced from a citable Census PEP release. Adequate for flagging outlier years; replace before publishing any derived figure as a headline number.
